newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares up slightly on speculative buys.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares up slightly on speculative buys.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index shed early sharp gains and closed only marginally higher on Tuesday due in part to speculative buying by institutions despite heavy profit-taking, brokers said.
The B index rose 1.70 points, or 1.27 percent, to end at 135.14 after touching an intraday high of 147.70 on turnover of HK$415.10 million, compared with Monday's HK$347.13 million.
Brokers said the market was dominated by speculative trading by institutions on Tuesday, with share prices fluctuating in a wider range.
"The surge was due to speculative buying by institutions," a broker at a major Chinese brokerage said.

"Heavy profit-taking pushed the index off its day high. The index still has space to go up if there is no official denial of rumours that Beijing is considering market-boosting plans," said the broker at China Southern Securities.
"With the index having gained about 50 percent over the past few sessions, the risk has become gradually higher," one analyst said.
"The recent surprising bullishness of the market has resulted in an inflow of hot money," another analyst said.
Conglomerate Gintian, the session's star, soared HK$0.45, or 10.23 percent, to HK$4.85 on volume of 1.56 million shares due to speculative purchasing.

Television tube maker Baoshi rose HK$0.45, or 10.14 percent, to HK$4.89 on trade of 3.30 million shares. Chiwan Wharf followed with a rise of HK$0.57, or 9.53 percent, to HK$6.55 on volume of 1.15 million shares.
Dadonghai traded the second most on volume of 6.81 million shares, inching up HK$0.01 to HK$3.14.
Changan Automobile remained the focus of institutional trading, losing HK$0.02 to HK$3.21 after hitting an intraday high of HK$3.60 on heavy trade of 15.19 million shares.
Weifu, the worst performer, fell HK$0.43, or 8.87 percent, to HK$4.42 as 1.10 million shares changed hands due to profit-taking, brokers said.

The A market edged lower on profit-taking, brokers said. The A share index shed 4.94 points, or 1.08 percent, to end at 452.50 on turnover of 15.77 billion yuan, compared with 16.36 billion yuan the previous session.
The composite index dipped 4.22 points, or 0.98 percent, to 425.02.
Chemical fibre maker Kunshan Sanshan slumped 0.62 yuan, or 5.65 percent, to 10.35 yuan. Nanyou Property dipped 1.15 yuan, or 5.31 percent, to 20.50 yuan.
